correctness.rationale: Finite Rees representation partitions nonzero elements into group H-classes or square-zero cells. A square-zero source element maps to a quotient annihilator: if a product is nonregular, its reverse is zero; if regular, its image is simultaneously group-valued and square-zero and hence zero. When both cross entries of two regular source classes are nonzero, their triple sandwich products force the two quotient group identities equal; if either cross entry vanishes, their products vanish. These cover both source-zero and source-zero-free cases. Explicit Brandt embedding supplies converse. 3616 quotient instances in the attached checker corroborate, not prove, the general argument.

value.rationale: The 2026 notebook explicitly separates Brandt and zero-one Rees source classes in a structural divisor problem. The theorem shows that, for every finite commutative target, the two apparently different HS problems collapse to one rigid normal form, and in fact this holds for arbitrary finite Rees sandwich groups and matrices. This is a motivated complete classification on an infinite natural family, not a small computed parameter or a routine restatement of Rees representation.
